status: Paraphrases of uncorroborated interview allegations; audio not independently verified.

scenes.title: A mother. A baby. A disputed removal.
scenes.body: Woods describes a mother who cared for her baby, family conflict that had been resolved, and several agencies already involved.
scenes.meaning: Start with the family’s circumstances—not the later labels.
scenes.check: Original assessments, agency records and the family’s account.

scenes.title: The first court said no.
scenes.body: She says the magistrates rejected the authority’s attempt to obtain an order to put the baby in care or remove her.
scenes.meaning: The authority did not obtain the outcome it sought at that hearing.
scenes.check: The application, magistrates’ order and hearing record.

scenes.title: Then, she says, came a request to change the file.
scenes.body: After that court outcome, Woods says a legal representative asked her to alter the child’s file to favor the local authority. She says she refused.
scenes.meaning: This is the crucial alleged turn: change the evidence after the first attempt fails.
scenes.check: Contemporaneous notes, file versions, correspondence and the other party’s response.

scenes.title: The proceedings continued.
scenes.body: Woods describes the case being pursued in another court and the strain on a young mother with little personal support.
scenes.meaning: An initial favorable outcome did not end the mother’s ordeal, in this account.
scenes.check: Later applications, hearing dates, orders and the family’s account.

scenes.title: Other people had seen the evidence.
scenes.body: She describes probation involvement, an NSPCC assessment of the father, and a guardian examining her records and responding positively.
scenes.meaning: The story identifies other records and a witness who could test what the file contained.
scenes.check: The assessments, guardian’s report and copies of the file reviewed.

scenes.title: She refused. Then left the case.
scenes.body: Woods says she refused to alter records, resigned, and was removed from the case. She says the mother was not allowed to speak with her.
scenes.meaning: The professional challenging the record was allegedly separated from the family and case.
scenes.check: Resignation and assignment records, contact instructions and their stated reasons.

scenes.title: The guardian allegedly challenged the mismatch.
scenes.body: Woods says she was later told that the guardian challenged material presented as her account because it did not match the files he had seen. She also recounts a judicial rebuke.
scenes.meaning: A claimed contradiction between the original record and what reached court.
scenes.check: The guardian’s evidence, court bundle and hearing transcript. Woods says this was related to her later.

scenes.title: What if evidence of institutional harm disappears?
scenes.body: In a separate passage, Woods alleges that crucial documents recording harm caused by authorities were removed from children’s files.
scenes.meaning: The alleged omission changes whose conduct the remaining record reveals.
scenes.check: Original and later file inventories, version histories and the formal complaints she describes.

scenes.title: What remains can change the story.
scenes.body: She then alleges that altered material was used in court. The interview does not establish which particular court bundle contained each missing document.
scenes.meaning: A record can appear complete even when the evidence needed to challenge it is missing.
scenes.check: Compare the original records with the actual court bundles. Do not assume this was the same baby’s case.
